_meta.note: Data table for bin/route.mjs (the routing bundle). Three grids, all editable without touching code: `cells` keys on (stakes level, role) and yields the model and the two rungs, `review` keys on (level, trigger) and yields a gate, `verify` keys on the level alone. Models are Claude dispatch aliases (opus/sonnet/haiku/fable) - stable, not dated ids, so no staleness. Effort is fixed per agent FILE in frontmatter, so varying it means varying the file: a cell's rung names a file, and cadence-core/bin/lib/rung-agent.mjs says which.
_meta.rungs: A rung costs an agent file, and every registered agent's name/description/tools ride in the main session prompt - so the reachable rungs are exactly the ones some cell names, not a rung_order x roles cross product. The rung -> filename map is stated per role in cadence-core/bin/lib/rung-agent.mjs (it cannot be derived: the analyzer's unsuffixed file is its xhigh rung), and self-verify fails in BOTH directions - a cell naming a rung with no file, and a rung file no cell reaches.
_meta.cells: The (stakes level, role) grid: one cell per pair, each yielding the `model` the role runs at, the `effort` rung it starts at and the `retry` rung a failed attempt climbs to. 18 cells, read in one screen - `tier` is gone, and with it the indirection that pinned a role's model to a field named after something else. A `retry` at or above its `effort` is the rule self-verify enforces; equal means the rung is held.
_meta.roles: The declared ARRAY of routable role names, and what route.mjs checks a `--role` against.
_meta.review: The `review` grid keys on (stakes level, trigger name) and yields the gate that trigger fires at, for the five triggers config.schema.json defines. `risk_surface` is deliberately `blocking` at EVERY level: it fires only on a detection match, so there is no level at which a matched risk surface is worth waving through. A `review.triggers.<t>.gate` a user set wins over the level's value and route.mjs reports the disagreement in `warnings`.
_meta.verify: The `verify` grid keys on the stakes level ALONE - the deep-verify pass has no role in hand when it decides whether to run. It is two-state (`off`/`on`); the depth of that pass is carried by the cad-verifier row of the effort grid, not here.
_meta.surfaces: The declared risk surfaces. A row's `patterns` are lowercase tokens matched for EQUALITY against the tokens of a path the phase's PLAN declares in its `files:` frontmatter; a match RAISES the resolved stakes level to that row's `floor` and never lowers it (the comparison order is `stakes_order`). `risk.override.<surface>` is the per-surface waiver: the floor drops back to the baseline only when every detected surface is named. Patterns are data - moving one is an edit here, not a code change - and self-verify walks the block against config.schema.json in both directions.
_meta.gates: The accepted `review.triggers.<t>.gate` vocabulary, checked by route.mjs before a config-set gate may win over the level's gate - the same role model_aliases plays for a pin, in the same file, so the resolver never reads config.schema.json.
_meta.aliases: model_aliases is the accepted vocabulary for a `model.overrides.<role>` pin. The ROUTED vocabulary is narrower - `sonnet` and `opus` - so `haiku` and `fable` are reachable by a pin only. For `fable` that is not a ranking claim: it requires 30-day data retention and returns 400 invalid_request_error for every zero-data-retention org, which is other people's orgs since Cadence ships as a public plugin; its safety classifiers return a refusal stop reason on cyber-adjacent content, and Cadence reviews its own git rails, secrets handling and shell tokenizer; and its multi-minute turns press against the configured provider request timeout inside the host's Bash ceiling. It is reachable only by explicit pin, which is a user assertion about their own org, not ours.
